1: Sunlight reaches the Moon in just 8 minutes!
2: The Sun is so big that a million Earths could fit inside it.
3: Northern lights glow when solar particles touch Earth's air.
4: The Moon has no air, so it's silent there — astronauts talk by radio.
5: A solar cloud reaches the Moon in a few days — faster than any rocket!
6: Dark spots on the Sun are places where it's a bit cooler.
7: NASA scientists photograph the Sun from space every day.
8: On the Moon you weigh 6 times less — you can hop like a kangaroo!
9: The Moon always shows the same side to Earth.
10: One solar cloud weighs as much as a whole mountain!
11: A day on the Moon lasts almost two weeks.
12: Moon dust is sharp and sticky, like tiny bits of glass.
13: The first astronauts' footprints are still on the Moon — nothing wipes them away.
14: In the daytime the Moon gets hotter than boiling water!
15: A lunar night lasts two weeks and is colder than the North Pole.
16: From the Moon, Earth looks like a big blue marble in the sky.
17: A strong solar flare can disturb radios on Earth.
18: Without radio contact, astronauts rely on the forecast they got earlier.
19: The Sun spins like a top: one turn takes about a month.
20: An invisible magnetic shield protects Earth from solar particles, but the Moon has none.
21: Some spots on the Sun are many times bigger than Earth!
22: The Sun gets calm and then angry again, in a cycle of about 11 years.
23: The fastest solar particles fly at nearly the speed of light!
24: In May 2024, northern lights were seen even in Ukraine!
25: The best shield from radiation is a thick layer of soil or water.
26: Astronauts wear small devices that count radiation.
27: There is water on the Moon — ice in dark craters.
28: The Moon moves 4 cm farther from Earth every year — as fast as nails grow!
29: Leaving the Moon is easier than leaving Earth: everything weighs 6 times less.
30: People first walked on the Moon in 1969 — and they'll go back soon!
31: The tallest mountain in the Solar System is on Mars — almost three times taller than Everest.
32: On Venus, one day is longer than a whole year!
33: Jupiter is so big that more than a thousand Earths could fit inside it.
34: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.
35: The International Space Station circles Earth in an hour and a half.
36: The first artificial satellite flew in 1957.
37: The Hubble telescope has photographed space from orbit since 1990.
38: The James Webb telescope sees light from the oldest stars.
39: In space, astronauts 'grow' a little — up to 5 cm!
40: The space station crew sees 16 sunrises every day.
41: On Mars the daytime sky is pink, and sunsets are blue.
42: Comets are giant dirty snowballs made of ice and dust.
43: 'Shooting stars' are tiny grains burning up high in the air.
44: The hottest stars glow blue, and cooler ones glow red.
45: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, has over 100 billion stars.
46: On Neptune the winds are faster than a jet plane.
47: The Moon has no weather: no rain, no wind, no clouds.
48: A spacesuit protects an astronaut from cold, heat and dust.
49: Plants in space grow under special lamps.
50: In space, people eat from pouches so crumbs don't float around.
